itens.titulo: Coca-Cola Bets $10 Billion on U.S. Infrastructure to Drive Growth
itens.descricao: Coca-Cola Bets $10 Billion on U.S. Infrastructure to Drive Growth Yahoo Finance
trechos: The Coca-Cola Company (NYSE:KO) plans to invest $10 billion in U.S.
infrastructure from 2026 through 2030, reinforcing its manufacturing, distribution, and bottling network in one of its most important markets.
The commitment is system-wide and therefore includes investments by Coca-Cola's bottling partners, rather than representing $10 billion of Coca-Cola's own capital expenditure.
The early-2026 trajectory makes that potential more significant.
Coca-Cola subsequently raised its 2026 organic revenue-growth outlook to approximately 5% and comparable EPS growth to 9%-10%.

Heavy Infrastructure Spending Could Pressure Returns and Cash Flow The headline $10 billion figure could overstate the direct financial benefit to The Coca-Cola Company (NYSE:KO) shareholders because the commitment includes bottling partners.

Coca-Cola's own 2026 capital expenditure is expected to be substantially smaller, so investors should not assume that the entire $10 billion will appear on Coca-Cola's balance sheet or generate returns directly attributable to the company.
In 2025, North American unit-case volume declined 1% despite a 5% price/mix benefit, highlighting the possibility that pricing rather than underlying consumption remains the primary growth lever.
